contents.entry: The run: one shot, input to output, limits, the launch argv (#launch-flags), result
Store access: none for a seat; the launcher writes under the lease
Roles, where an LLM appears, the reviewer
Credentials and the verdict a seat cannot edit
Owner-side clauses: break glass, relay, lanes, halt, standing policies, keys
Build mode as the seat sees it

pointers.shared: N-15 is the code that honours this contract
N-13 renders the settings this contract names
N-30 holds the routing table the lanes clause summarises
Principals, isolation, credentials, owner words: what this contract defers to
The lease states, fencing and the terminal-report exception

purpose.s: A seat is one bounded process of a model between an input record and an output record (D02 C36, D17 C49); this contract is the whole of what it may rely on and the whole of what the system may expect of it.
Node volumes cite clauses by anchor; the launcher (N-15), the fence (N-13), the validator (N-18) and the audit (N-51) are the code that enforces them; a clause with no enforcing node is a defect.

clause.title: One shot: bundle plus workspace in, seat.result out
clause.rule: A seat is one bounded process between a seat.bundle plus workspace record and a seat.result record; no pane, no prompt, no nudge, no idle state, no second turn from outside.
A launcher restart adopts a live run into the same beat loop against the same absolute deadline_at, never a new bound (principles.xml#no-cog).
The seat exists only between the two records (dag.md section 1); a run that ends without a seat.result is written as blocked by the launcher with terminal_reason no_result.
clause.check: N-15 test: kill the launcher mid-run; the restarted launcher finds the pid, adopts it, and the deadline is unchanged.

clause.title: A fresh seat per attempt
clause.rule: Every attempt, rework or follow-up brings up a fresh seat (owner 2026-10-13 02:02Z: every agent is a cog and nobody is a gate) as a fresh pool user (authority.xml#seat-isolation); whether a rework resumes the previous session (--resume with a new brief carrying the verdict) or starts fresh is decided only by contracts.xml#retry-owner; either way it is a new run with its own lease, deadline and seat.result.
Nothing is typed into a running seat; the verdict is in the brief, so no wake can be lost (S04 section 8 item 8).

clause.title: The brief is the input
clause.rule: The brief (brief.md in the bundle) is the only input the model reads at start; it is rendered by N-13 from the ticket record, the role and the repository, never typed.
A brief names the input record that started the run and the output record that ends it; a seat that cannot produce the output posts a blocked object and leaves.

clause.title: brief.md sections in order
clause.rule: ticket (id and full title, never a bare id); input and output; files (the declared set, the fence); acceptance with observed exits on main; steps; rules (the principles anchors); verdict on a retry; limits once as information.
clause.check: N-13 test: the rendered brief has exactly these headings in this order; a role template with another heading fails render.

clause.title: Limits are fields, never prose
clause.rule: max_turns, max_budget_usd, wall_clock_seconds and stall_seconds are role schema fields (rebuild/roles/*.json shape) and launcher arguments; the model never counts them; the launcher kills at the bound (killed_deadline, killed_stall).
Defaults by role live in the role file; a dispatch may lower, never raise, a limit.

clause.title: The launch argv comes only from the list below
clause.rule: The launcher (N-15) builds argv only from the arg elements of #launch-flags, in order, and passes it to coq-seat-exec start (authority.xml#principals); no other source of flags exists, and N-15 and N-13 cite this list instead of restating it.

Never --fallback-model (a silent model swap is an unrecorded decision); never --permission-mode bypassPermissions or --dangerously-skip-permissions (under bypass an allow rule restricts nothing, so the fence would be prose; dontAsk makes a miss a recorded denial); never --no-session-persistence in any form, because a resume rework needs the session file.

Before every spawn the launcher checks the resolved harness against the pin (path, version, sha256 of the binary); any difference is seat.result blocked 412 terminal_reason harness_mismatch and no process starts. claude --version alone proves nothing about the argv (it exits 0 even beside an unknown flag), so the golden envelopes are the proof.
clause.check: Golden envelopes, run on the host and in the pod image before any harness pin changes, each against the pinned binary with this argv: success; forbidden-path denial (permission_denials names the path, nothing changes on disk); invalid structured output; max turns; max budget; a user hook, a workspace CLAUDE.md and an MCP server outside mcp.json that must not load; resume of a saved session. Status: not-run.

harness.sha256: recorded by the pin ticket from the host binary
harness.note: 2.1.300 is the version read in the design container on 2026-10-15; the pin ticket records the host's own

arg.with: the text of BUNDLE/brief.md as one argument

arg.note: host and pod seats: skips hooks, plugins, auto-memory, keychain and CLAUDE.md discovery; auth is then ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or apiKeyHelper only (authority.xml#credential-matrix row anthropic-seat)

arg.with: BUNDLE/settings.json (the fence N-13 renders; carries apiKeyHelper on the host)

arg.note: beside --bare, never instead of it: keeps the workspace's project and user settings files out of the permission set
confirmed by claude --help 2.1.300: choices host or none; none denies anything that would prompt
absent from --help 2.1.300; kept only if the max-turns golden envelope passes (not-run)

arg.with: the compact JSON text of the node's output schema (one argument, no path; the help example passes JSON text); N-13 refuses to render a schema over 120 KiB because one argv string is capped at 128 KiB

env.note: HOME is the pool user's home; PATH holds the pinned tool directory only; COQ_SEAT=RUN_ID is a diagnostic label, never authority

clause.title: Structured output against the node's schema
clause.rule: Every phase returns structured output against the node's record.schema.json through --json-schema; an optional blocked object carries reason, observations and repro.
The launcher validates structured_output again with its own validator; two disagreeing validators are launcher.defect 500 (status-codes.xml#code-500).

clause.title: seat.result comes from the harness
clause.rule: seat.result is parsed by the launcher from the claude -p JSON envelope (type result, subtype, is_error, total_cost_usd, num_turns, session_id, structured_output, permission_denials); a seat never posts its own result; a model's claim is data to verify.

Outcomes: done 200 with validated structured output; blocked 423 with a terminal_reason from the table (success, error_max_turns, error_max_budget_usd, error_during_execution, error_max_structured_output_retries, killed_deadline, killed_stall, killed_lease_lost, killed_by_record, crashed, no_result, schema_invalid, output_rejected, seat_blocked); blocked 412 on a preflight miss (bundle_mismatch, workspace_mismatch, lease_not_current, claim_missing, harness_mismatch); 412 is the only preflight code (status-codes.xml#code-412).

clause.title: What seat.result carries
clause.rule: The shape is nodes/N-15/record.schema.json#/$defs/seat.result and nothing else: run_id, ticket, role, phase, attempt, outcome, code, terminal_reason, session_id, model, started_at, finished_at, duration_seconds, cost_usd, turns, permission_denials, result_path, stderr_path, plus lease (contracts.schema.json#/$defs/lease_ref), fenced (true only under contracts.xml#terminal-report), denied_line_ops {count, commands} for every role, and phase_record_ref, the id of the record the phase produced (the worker's pr.opened written by N-16 close-out, the spec author's ticket-set.draft, the reviewer's review record).
N-11 reads it as the failure record when the outcome is not done (contracts.schema.json#/$defs/failure_body); N-51 sums denied_line_ops into row A2.

clause.title: The lease is the launcher's, never the seat's
clause.rule: A seat holds no lease token, no store socket and no store path (authority.xml#seat-isolation); the launcher carries the run's lease (key and token) on every Commit it makes for the run, and a token that is not current is 412 stale_token or lease_not_current (contracts.xml#fencing), except the one terminal report contracts.xml#terminal-report accepts.
A kind outside the launcher's permit row is 403 record.refused kind_not_permitted (authority.xml#role-derivation), whatever the token.

clause.title: What a seat may call
clause.rule: Nothing of the store: everything a seat needs is in its bundle (brief.md, ticket.json, the diff and gate status for a reviewer), and its only output is the structured output the launcher parses; there is no seat.note and no record add.
seat.heartbeat, seat.result and phase.failed are the launcher's Commits, not the seat's.
clause.check: A seat process opening /run/coq/store.sock gets EACCES (authority.xml#proofs).

clause.title: The launcher renews the lease
clause.rule: The launcher (N-15), not the model, starts and renews the lease on the cadence of contracts.xml#timing; the heartbeat entity carries the lease_ref (key, token, generation), pid, progress_at, transcript_bytes and adopted.
Stall and expiry follow contracts.xml#lease-machine and the stall bounds of contracts.xml#timing; the kill is contracts.xml#kill-authority.

clause.title: The ticket as data
clause.rule: id, title (never a bare id), files, deps, role, acceptance commands with expected exit codes and observed_exit_on_main, input, output, priority, lane, set_id, hold_id when it is a fix ticket; the seat reads it from ticket.json in its bundle and never changes it.
A ticket is cut by N-17 as data and admitted only after N-18 ran its acceptance commands on main (D16 C48).

clause.title: Roles
clause.rule: worker (N-16), spec-author (N-17), reviewer (N-19), screenshot (N-48, no model). Tester, merger and verifier roles are retired: code does them (D11 C39; N-24, N-09, N-26).

The worker run ends with its commits in the workspace and N-16 close-out writes pr.opened (head_sha, head_repo, pr, ticket), named by seat.result.phase_record_ref; the reviewer posts review.passed or review.changes on the head sha independent of the gate; the spec author ends with ticket-set.draft.

clause.title: An LLM appears only for judgement
clause.rule: An LLM appears only in N-16 (write code), N-17 (cut tickets as data) and N-19 (judge a diff); every mechanical step around it is code (principles.xml#code-does-mechanical-jobs).

clause.title: The reviewer is a separate run
clause.rule: The reviewer shares no session and no workspace with the writer, runs nothing (no build, no test), never holds the gh write, and reads the diff, the gate status and the ticket only.
Right-size: a role's model is the role file's model or Sonnet; no Opus or Fable seat without a ruling (memory right-size-agent-models).

clause.title: The review record
clause.rule: review.passed 201 or review.changes 422 carries pr, ticket, head_sha, lease (lease_ref), run_id and the findings, written by N-19 from the reviewer's seat.result under operation key N-19/review.verdict/PR@HEAD_SHA@RUN_ID/r1 (contracts.xml#operation-keys); a stale lease is 412; N-09 merges only on the newest review.passed for the current head sha.

clause.title: Local proof a worker may run
clause.rule: A worker may run factory/bin/suites.sh plan, ci/bin/plan-units.sh --dry, ci/image/build.sh --no-push and bin/test-cases.sh locally; none touches a registry, Jenkins or the cluster; the gate's verdict is the pods', not the worker's.

clause.title: A mechanical pull request
clause.rule: A system-authored pull request that changes exactly one declared data file (the GitHub egress CIDR bump in homelab-gitops, N-22) merges on gate green without a reviewer record; any other PR needs review.passed.

clause.title: Credential by placement
clause.rule: Every credential, its holder and its storage is one row of authority.xml#credential-matrix; a seat holds only the Anthropic seat credential, through apiKeyHelper on the host or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in a pod, and never prints or copies it.
The ghcr push token and the homelab-gitops deploy key stay in Jenkins and the Argo cluster; the service's own credentials are coq-svc's files under STATE/secrets and never appear in a record.

clause.title: Forge access from a seat
clause.rule: A seat never pushes and never opens a pull request: it commits in its workspace and ends; N-16's close-out code, as coq-svc with forge-pr, pushes the branch and opens the PR after the seat.result (authority.xml#credential-matrix); the seat's network reaches no forge (authority.xml#seat-isolation).

clause.title: The verdict is read-only (T04)
clause.rule: Seats hold no forge, Jenkins or cluster credential and reach none of them; the rendered settings also deny gh, git push, kubectl, jenkins-mcp and the kubernetes MCP tools for every role, so a try is a permission denial counted in denied_line_ops, never a write.

The deny list also covers make serve, wait, stop, upgrade and front-door; systemctl --user; cleanup.sh apply; unlanded.sh apply; publish-drive.sh; promote.sh; Reload; git push to main; gh pr merge and close; branch delete; $COQ_STATE/secrets.

clause.title: Line operations are never a seat's
clause.rule: A seat never writes code.table, build-mode.state, rule.bit, cleanup.run, disposition, cancel, pr.close, branch.delete, promotion, exit.verdict, freeze.state or any flag; no seat can commit anything, and the launcher's permit row excludes these kinds (403 kind_not_permitted, authority.xml#role-derivation); seat.result.denied_line_ops counts every denied command; N-51 row A1 must be zero for the day.

clause.title: The screenshot seat
clause.rule: The screenshot seat (N-48) holds only the viewer key, read-only, no action rendered; Playwright at 1440 and 430 widths; writes only under $COQ_STATE/map/screenshots/; its screenshot record is the proof a promotion carries (memory screenshot-every-page-change).

clause.title: Owner key and viewer key
clause.rule: The owner key and viewer key work as nodes/N-32/spec.xml#web-security specifies; only an owner session renders an action; the viewer key draws read-only; no seat holds either key or writes a control.action, ruling, hold flag or token; a seat needing a ruling ends blocked (seat_blocked) and N-28 builds the card from its blocked object; the key is never in a record (memory bearings-restart-and-page-key).

clause.title: Break glass: owner-only, one time
clause.rule: Every break glass verb is owner-only and one time: a token minted by a ruling on a card (N-29), consumed by compare-and-swap, recorded as control.action with origin break-glass or as a cutover record; only an owner principal may use it (authority.xml#role-derivation), any other caller is control.refused 403; N-51 counts every such record as a hand line operation for that day (row A3).

The list: promote.sh --tier stable --sha; systemctl --user start coq-cutover@PAGE; rotate-key; cleanup-tier on stable; unlanded.sh apply; cleanup.sh apply outside a plan. When the page is unreachable the same record is posted through the owner CLI on the host (owner principal, authority.xml#peer-credentials) and read back before acting.

clause.title: An owner answer relayed from chat or the phone
clause.rule: A relayed answer is recorded verbatim as owner.answer with source relay through the owner CLI, and may carry only the relayable effects of authority.xml#relayable-rulings (none, ticket.unblock); every other effect, the owner words above all, is refused (answer.rejected 403 not_relayable) and the card stays open (authority.xml#owner-words).
No dispatched role may relay: seats have no socket; N-51 counts relays as owner acts by channel.

clause.title: Message lanes
clause.rule: Lanes: control, ticket, card, sitrep, architect, system, unroutable. Rules in order (N-30): R01 USERHALT, R02 USERGO and R03 GOFACTORY to control, N-29, 5 s, each only when the whole trimmed message is the word from an owner principal (authority.xml#owner-words; USERGO before bootstrap state B7 is control.refused 412 not-ready naming the missing proofs, cut-over.xml#bootstrap; GOFACTORY one time); R04 a reply to a card id to card, N-29, 5 s; R05 cut: or ticket: to ticket, N-03, 60 s; R06 sitrep or status to sitrep, 30 s; R07 system: to system, N-06, 30 s; R08 a PR URL or ticket id to the architect digest, 1800 s; R99 anything else to the architect digest, 1800 s; the architect lane's consumer is the N-30 digest builder (code), which consumes at once and answers with a templated reply at the sla when no reply came (nodes/N-30/spec.xml#mechanism step 3).

A lane's SLA is a wait with a bounded fallback (the stale receipt for a node consumer, the templated reply for the architect lane); the architect is a digest lane and never a prompt target (K01, the 2026-10-13 flood); the owner's architect session reads the digest with coq inbox digest under the owner's host CLI identity and may relay only per #relay.

clause.title: Halt and resume
clause.rule: USERHALT is a hold and only a hold: it sets flag:hold, which refuses GrantDispatch and work-class leases (contracts.xml#lease-machine); running seats finish their bound; ticks, health, backups, the poll, the push transport, the stable page, its watcher and its front door never stop; line.halted 503 and line.resumed 100 each become one card.

Stopping a running seat is a separate owner-only action (the Controls kill of N-42 on one run, or on all runs): N-12 writes kill:RUN_ID and the launcher stops the unit (contracts.xml#kill-authority); USERHALT never kills.

clause.title: Standing policies a card builder applies
clause.rule: No bare ticket id (always id dash full title); one question per card; a recommendation always named; a default and a deadline only on a relayable card (V17), never on an owner-only card (authority.xml#relayable-rulings); the Krastorio look on the card; bad news first, 15 words a line, no semicolon in a bubble (STD-owner-comms-001).
Claimed items are never re-raised (CLAUDE.md: once I claim something, it is mine); a card about one is refused 400 by N-28's rule check.

clause.title: Build mode as the seat sees it
clause.rule: A seat reads build mode only from its dispatch record, in the one shape contracts.schema.json#/$defs/build_mode (on, scope, version, expires_at, ruling_ref), never from a flag it queries; a seat bundle under build mode omits every old-line hook, guard, watch, AutoMem and prettier PostToolUse, and the bundle hash input includes build_mode and scope (N-13, N-44).
A refusal that names an old rule under build mode is rule.bit 300, not an attempt (principles.xml#build-mode).

many-agents.readers: Every seat's brief carries the anchors of this contract it is bound by; twenty seats run under it at once because nothing in it is shared state: each has its own lease token, workspace slot, deadline and result key.
many-agents.writers: The launcher is the only writer of seat.heartbeat and seat.result, keyed by run_id; one launcher per run holds because the transient unit coq-seat-RUN_ID is unique by name and the run:RUN_ID entity moves by compare-and-swap (contracts.xml#run-states), so a second launcher instance loses the swap and adopts or leaves.
many-agents.collision: Two seats on one ticket phase cannot exist: the lease admits one reserved or running holder (contracts.xml#lease-machine); a stale token on any Commit is 412; two review runs on one head sha are two records keyed N-19/review.verdict/PR@HEAD_SHA@RUN_ID/r1, and N-09 reads the newest.
